name: Duolingo — Responsible AI Standards
dinh_nghia: Duolingo operates two distinct AI postures that coexist within the same company: (1) AI IS the learning product — the Duolingo language learning app uses generative AI extensively for personalized instruction, conversation practice, and adaptive content generation; (2) AI is BANNED as a cheating vector in the Duolingo English Test (DET) — a high-stakes English proficiency certification used by 5,000+ universities globally for admissions. The DET's 'Responsible AI Standards' (first published April 2023, updated annually) govern how AI is used ethically in the exam context, including human-in-the-loop proctoring and an LLM cheating detection system detailed in an EMNLP 2024 paper.
phan_loai: Duolingo's AI integrity framework specifically targets: (1) LLM-assisted cheating on open-ended writing tasks — test-takers who use AI to generate responses and copy-type them into the DET interface; (2) Cheating rings — coordinated networks of test-takers sharing answers (separate AI system, arXiv 2403.14711); (3) Identity fraud — proctoring verifies the registered test-taker is present; (4) Traditional cheating behaviors — looking away from screen, using secondary devices. The learning app context addresses AI as tutor; the DET context addresses AI as cheater.
lich_su_khai_niem: Duolingo English Test launched in 2016 as a low-cost alternative to IELTS/TOEFL. During COVID-19 (2020–2022), DET adoption surged as test centers closed — by 2021, 5,000+ universities accepted DET. The AI integrity challenge became acute with ChatGPT's release (November 2022): test-takers could use LLMs to generate English writing that they then typed into the DET interface. Duolingo published the first DET Responsible AI Standards in April 2023. The EMNLP 2024 paper (Niu et al.) represents the first peer-reviewed publication of the LLM cheating detection methodology. Duolingo's learning app introduced AI features (DuolingoMax, GPT-4 powered Roleplay and Explain My Answer) in 2023.
ten_truong_hop: Duolingo English Test Responsible AI Standards, first published April 2023. LLM cheating detection paper: 'Detecting LLM-Assisted Cheating on Open-Ended Writing Tasks on Language Proficiency Tests' (Niu et al., EMNLP 2024 Industry Track, ACL Anthology 2024.emnlp-industry.70). Security and Score Integrity Report published by Duolingo Research. Responsible AI for Test Equity and Quality paper (arXiv:2409.07476, 2024).
dien_bien: DET Responsible AI Standards (2023/2024): Duolingo defined four major standards categories — (1) Validity and Reliability, (2) Fairness, (3) Privacy and Security, (4) Accountability and Transparency. Human-in-the-loop AI proctoring: AI monitors video, audio, and on-screen behavior to flag anomalies; all flagged cases are reviewed by human proctors before any certification decision. AI is used to compare test-taker writing responses against a database of internet content and historical DET writing responses, with matches flagged for human review. LLM cheating detection (EMNLP 2024): researchers developed a transformer-based classifier enhanced with contrastive learning on pairwise data and self-training on unlabeled data. The key challenge addressed: LLM-generated text that has been copy-typed by the test-taker (introducing typos and variations) is harder to detect than clean AI output. Evaluated on real-world DET dataset. The improved model outperformed baseline classifiers.
ket_qua_xu_ly: Certified DET scores are only issued when both AI proctoring and human review confirm validity. Test-takers flagged for LLM-assisted cheating have their results invalidated and may be banned from retaking the DET. Duolingo does not publicly disclose the number of invalidated scores per year. [uncertain] The DET Security Report describes the multi-layer review process without quantifying outcomes. The LLM detection system (EMNLP 2024) showed improved accuracy over baseline in real-world testing, but precision and recall figures on the published dataset are not separately disclosed for exam conditions. [uncertain]
con_so_thong_ke: 5,000+ universities accept DET scores globally (2024). DET is taken in 200+ countries. Duolingo app: 500+ million downloads; 100+ million monthly active users (2024). Number of DET test-takers per year: not publicly disclosed. [uncertain] EMNLP 2024 paper: the improved LLM detection model 'outperforms the original transformer-based classifier and other baselines' on the real-world DET dataset — specific F1/AUC numbers not cited in public summaries. [uncertain]
hai_cho_nguoi_hoc: For DET test-takers: the multi-layer integrity system means genuine test-takers with strong English proficiency should not be penalized. However, false positive risk exists — a test-taker who writes unusually fluent English may be flagged as potentially AI-assisted. The human-in-the-loop review process is intended to catch such cases before score invalidation, but the process is not fully transparent to test-takers. For Duolingo app users: AI features are beneficial — GPT-4 powered Roleplay and Explain My Answer are pedagogically valuable without integrity risks in a non-high-stakes context.
hai_cho_nghien_cuu: The EMNLP 2024 paper by Niu et al. is a significant research contribution: it is among the first peer-reviewed studies of LLM cheating detection on real-world high-stakes language test data (not synthetic). The contrastive learning + self-training approach for copy-typed AI text detection advances the state of the art. The arXiv:2409.07476 paper ('Responsible AI for Test Equity and Quality') provides a framework applicable beyond Duolingo to other high-stakes AI-assisted assessments.
hai_cho_xa_hoi: The DET's integrity is critical for the university admissions process: 5,000+ institutions rely on DET scores to admit international students. If DET scores are perceived as vulnerable to LLM cheating, the entire certification system collapses. Duolingo's published AI standards and EMNLP research serve to publicly demonstrate rigor, maintaining institutional trust. The responsible AI standards may also influence industry norms for other testing organizations (ETS, Cambridge, British Council).
cong_cu_phat_hien: Duolingo's DET detection stack: (1) Human-in-the-loop AI proctoring — AI monitors webcam, microphone, screen recording; anomalies flagged for human review; (2) Internet content matching — AI compares writing responses against database of online text; (3) Historical response matching — AI compares against database of prior DET submissions to detect recycled content; (4) LLM-generated text classifier (EMNLP 2024) — transformer-based model with contrastive learning, robust to copy-typed AI output; (5) Cheating ring detection (arXiv:2403.14711) — network analysis to identify coordinated cheating groups. All automated flags require human proctor review before action.
han_che_cong_cu: The LLM detection challenge for DET is specific: test-takers copy-type AI-generated content rather than pasting it directly, introducing variations that degrade traditional AI detection accuracy. The EMNLP 2024 paper addresses this but acknowledges that as LLMs improve, the detection-evasion arms race continues. Human-in-the-loop review introduces throughput constraints — if the volume of flagged cases is high, reviewer fatigue may reduce accuracy. Fairness concern: the 'Validity and Reliability' and 'Fairness' standards in the DET RAI framework explicitly address the risk that AI proctoring may be biased against test-takers with non-standard environments, connectivity issues, or physical differences in appearance.
watermarking: Duolingo's DET approach is not based on LLM watermarking. Watermarking (Kirchenbauer/UMD, Aaronson/OpenAI) would be useful for DET if AI providers embedded detectable signals in generated text — this would simplify detection of copy-typed AI content. However, watermarking is not yet universally implemented by LLM providers. Duolingo's current system (EMNLP 2024 classifier) operates without relying on watermarks, making it applicable in the current environment.
thiet_ke_bai_tap: The DET exam design itself is an integrity mechanism: the test includes speaking tasks, writing tasks, and interactive activities that must be completed in real time within a time limit, reducing (though not eliminating) the window for AI assistance. The exam includes adaptive questions that respond to test-taker performance, making preparation of fully AI-generated answers difficult. The combination of AI proctoring + LLM detection + human review is intended to make LLM-assisted cheating in the DET too risky and unreliable to attempt.
chinh_sach_truong_hoc: Duolingo English Test is accepted by 5,000+ institutions globally including Harvard, MIT, Stanford, and most major universities. Institutional acceptance depends on confidence in DET score validity — the published Responsible AI Standards and EMNLP research are intended to maintain this confidence. Institutions set their own minimum DET score requirements for admission. No university has publicly withdrawn DET acceptance specifically due to LLM cheating concerns as of 2025. [uncertain]
van_hoa_to_chuc: Duolingo's dual AI posture (AI-powered learning vs. AI-banned in exam) reflects a nuanced institutional stance: AI is a tool that should be used where it helps and banned where it undermines the assessment purpose. The publication of Responsible AI Standards and peer-reviewed research demonstrates a transparency and accountability culture. This contrasts with organizations that develop AI integrity tools without public disclosure of methods or limitations.
ai_literacy: Duolingo's app is explicitly designed to build AI literacy through use — students interact with AI conversation partners and receive AI-powered explanations, normalizing appropriate AI-assisted learning. The DET Responsible AI Standards publication educates the testing community about AI in high-stakes assessment contexts. Duolingo publishes detailed research reports (arXiv, EMNLP) that contribute to public understanding of LLM cheating detection — an important form of institutional AI literacy contribution.
khung_quoc_te: DET Responsible AI Standards align with: UNESCO 2023 guidance on responsible AI in education (validity, fairness, transparency, accountability); EU AI Act (2024) Annex III — high-stakes AI in education and vocational training; IEEE EAD (Ethics in Action Design); the four DET RAI categories (validity/reliability, fairness, privacy/security, accountability/transparency) map closely to OECD AI Principles and UNESCO's AI Ethics Recommendation. As a high-stakes admissions test, DET falls squarely within EU AI Act high-risk classification — Duolingo has not publicly addressed EU AI Act compliance in detail. [uncertain]
phap_luat_viet_nam: DET is accepted by Vietnamese universities and is used by Vietnamese students applying to international programs. Vietnam's Nghị định 109/2022/NĐ-CP focuses on scientific research integrity, not language proficiency testing. No MOET regulation specifically governs DET or similar online testing in Vietnam. The integrity mechanisms described in the DET Responsible AI Standards are relevant to Vietnam's broader discussion of AI use in standardized testing.
chinh_sach_chau_a: DET is widely used by Asian students for university admissions. NUS (Singapore), NTU (Singapore), and major Chinese, South Korean, and Japanese universities accept DET scores. The LLM cheating challenge is particularly acute in Asian markets where AI-assisted test preparation services are commercially available. Duolingo's EMNLP 2024 paper dataset includes real-world DET submissions from global test-takers including Asian candidates — providing one of the few large-scale datasets of LLM cheating in high-stakes Asian-relevant testing contexts.
ai_tutor_vs_ai_cheater: Duolingo is the clearest example of the AI-tutor-vs-AI-cheater tension within a single company's product portfolio. The Duolingo app embodies Rose Luckin's (UCL) democratizing AI tutor — making language learning accessible globally. The DET embodies Neil Selwyn's concern — AI enabling fraudulent credentials. Duolingo's response is not to choose one framing but to design each product context appropriately: AI-powered where it serves learning, AI-excluded where it undermines assessment validity. The Responsible AI Standards represent Duolingo's public articulation of this context-dependent policy.
edtech_company_policies: Duolingo two-context AI framework: (1) Duolingo App — AI IS the product: GPT-4 powered Roleplay (DuolingoMax), Explain My Answer, adaptive learning engine; AI used extensively to personalize instruction; no integrity concerns in informal learning context; (2) Duolingo English Test (DET) — AI is BANNED as a cheating vector: human-in-the-loop proctoring, LLM cheating detection (EMNLP 2024), internet content matching, historical response matching, cheating ring detection; all AI flags require human review; (3) Responsible AI Standards: four categories published April 2023, updated annually — Validity & Reliability, Fairness, Privacy & Security, Accountability & Transparency.
de_xuat_nha_nghien_cuu: From an EdTech researcher perspective: (1) Duolingo's dual AI posture should be a model for the industry: AI literacy tools (app) and high-stakes assessment (DET) require fundamentally different integrity frameworks; (2) The EMNLP 2024 paper by Niu et al. represents best practice for responsible disclosure of AI integrity system methodology — other EdTech companies should publish similar research; (3) The human-in-the-loop requirement for all AI flags is the correct approach for high-stakes decisions — automated-only decisions in high-stakes assessment are ethically problematic; (4) The contrastive learning approach for detecting copy-typed AI text should be evaluated for application in university plagiarism detection; (5) DET's Responsible AI Standards should be adopted as a template for other certification bodies (Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL) facing similar LLM cheating challenges.

[uncertain] The Springer 2024 study on AI use among 1,386 Vietnamese students provides relevant background — Vietnamese students represent a significant portion of DET test-takers. Vietnam context: the DET's accessibility (online, lower cost than IELTS/TOEFL) makes it particularly relevant to Vietnamese students applying abroad, heightening the importance of integrity assurance.
